questions.prompt: A bag-of-words style text encoder is tested on 100 forced-choice pairs 'A left of B' vs 'B left of A' for the same image. What accuracy do you expect?
options: About 100%, because the image alone decides which sentence matches it.
About 25%, because only one of four word orders can match the image.
It depends only on the image encoder size, not on how the text is encoded.
About 50%, because both sentences get the same embedding.
questions.explanation: Order-insensitive pooling gives identical text vectors, so the model cannot prefer either.

questions.prompt: Unit vectors u=(0.6,0.8) and v=(0.8,0.6). What is their cosine similarity? (2 decimals)
Two image-caption pairs with sim matrix [[0.8,0.6],[0.6,0.8]] and tau=0.5. What is the image-to-text InfoNCE loss? (3 decimals)
Reducing the temperature tau in the contrastive softmax does what?
options: Changes the number of negatives that appear in each contrastive batch.
Sharpens the softmax so margins between similarities are amplified.
Has no effect on the loss, since tau only rescales the final embedding.
Flattens the softmax toward uniform so margins between similarities shrink.
questions.explanation: Logits are s/tau; smaller tau amplifies differences.

questions.prompt: Prompt A is right only on 8 questions and prompt B only on 2 (all others agree). What is the exact two-sided sign-test p-value? (3 decimals)
Which analysis is appropriate for comparing two prompts evaluated on the same 60 questions?
options: A paired test on discordant questions (McNemar / exact sign test).
Average the two accuracies and report the mean as the common score.
Compare the two accuracies as if they came from independent samples.
Pick the prompt with the higher accuracy, since 60 questions are enough.
questions.explanation: Same questions mean paired data; only discordant pairs carry information.

questions.prompt: Design an evaluation of whether a vision-language model understands 'left of' for a robot. Specify the data, chance baseline, prompt variations and how you would report uncertainty.
rubric: Minimal pairs with swapped relations on the same images, with a stated chance level.
Several paraphrased prompts and a paired comparison.
Exact or bootstrap intervals and a falsifier fixed beforehand.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
